question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[\frac{1}{X}],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{5},\, & 2-y\le x\le \frac{y+4}{2},\,0\le y\le 2; \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability density function. If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={∬}_{{R}^{2}}r(x,y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=\frac{1}{x}.
$$

Now, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,2-y\le x\le \frac{y+4}{2}\},$ where $f(x,y)$ is nonzero.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14270831/assets/9dce6bf320cb848a36da0592645c0aca40b3c310a5f1394d8f7a0423ddd0ede6.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[5XY] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}\frac{1}{x}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{x}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{2-y}^{(y+4)/2}\frac{1}{x}\cdot \frac{x}{5}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{2-y}^{(y+4)/2}\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{2}[x]_{x=2-y}^{x=(y+4)/2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{y+4}{2}-(2-y))\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{3y}{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{10}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =\frac{3}{10}(2-0) \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
